locator: Utility Profile, Treatment and Distribution System, table Austin Water Treatment Plants and Capacity, p. 50 of 61; Water Supply System, p. 44 of 61
shows: The City of Austin's Water Conservation Plan of November 21, 2024 lists three surface water treatment plants of Austin Water: Davis (built 1954, 118 MGD), Ullrich (1969, 167 MGD) and Handcox (2014, 50 MGD). Their total treatment capacity is 335 MGD. Davis and Ullrich draw water from Lake Austin and Handcox from Lake Travis. The utility profile gives the designed capacity of the system as 335 MGD.
limits: These are rated design capacities, not the water that the plants can produce on a given day. The plan does not give a firm capacity with a plant or a unit out of service. All three plants take water from the Colorado River through its lakes.
